title: Classic Guacamole Avocado

description: This classic guacamole is a vibrant, creamy dip, bursting with the fresh flavors of ripe avocado, tangy lime, and aromatic cilantro. It is the quintessential Mexican appetizer, perfect for sharing with friends and family, offering a taste of authentic culinary tradition in every scoop. Simple to prepare, it is a guaranteed crowd-pleaser for any occasion.

ingredients.notes: seeded and finely minced (optional, for heat)

instructions.title: Prepare the Avocados
instructions.text: Halve the ripe avocados, remove the pits, and scoop the flesh into a medium mixing bowl. Mash the avocado with a fork or a potato masher to your desired consistency, leaving some chunks for texture.

instructions.title: Add Citrus and Seasoning
instructions.text: Immediately add the fresh lime juice to the mashed avocado. This helps prevent browning and adds a crucial tangy flavor. Sprinkle in the salt and mix gently to combine.

instructions.title: Incorporate Aromatics
instructions.text: Stir in the finely diced red onion and chopped fresh cilantro. If you are using jalapeño, add the finely minced pepper at this stage as well.

instructions.title: Add Optional Tomato
instructions.text: If desired, gently fold in the seeded and diced Roma tomato. Be careful not to overmix, as this can make the guacamole watery.

instructions.title: Taste and Adjust
instructions.text: Taste the guacamole and adjust seasonings as needed. You might want to add more salt, lime juice, or a pinch of extra jalapeño for more kick.

instructions.title: Serve Immediately
instructions.text: Transfer the classic guacamole to a serving bowl. For best results and to maintain its vibrant green color, serve immediately with tortilla chips, fresh vegetables, or as a topping for your favorite Mexican dishes.

tips: To prevent your guacamole from browning, press plastic wrap directly onto the surface of the guacamole before refrigerating. The lime juice also helps.
For the best flavor, use ripe Hass avocados. They should yield slightly to gentle pressure when squeezed. If they are too hard, they are not ready; if too soft, they might be overripe.
Serve your guacamole with warm, freshly made tortilla chips. A sprinkle of cotija cheese or a few extra cilantro sprigs can also enhance presentation.
